# Prior art — searched before designing, not after

## Bite / fraction-affected designs

**Haanwinckel (2024), arXiv 2307.01284, "Does regional variation in wage levels identify the
effects of a national minimum wage?"** The on-point methodological critique. Canonical exposures:

```
FA_r  = (1/I_r) Σ_i 1{ w_i0 < mw_1 }
Gap_r = Σ_i max{ mw_1 − w_i0, 0 } / Σ_i w_i0
```

Three named failure modes: (1) sensitivity to the functional form of the treatment-intensity
variable; (2) regression to the mean at the regional level, from sampling variation in regional
wage statistics and from region-specific productivity shocks; (3) trends in the dispersion of
latent wages (e.g. skill-biased technical change) violating parallel trends *even when they hit
every region identically*. Fix for (2) is the Dustmann et al. (2021) procedure — construct the
bite from a different pre-period than the one anchoring the outcome.

**The finding that cuts against this whole exercise:** Haanwinckel tests binarised
treatment-intensity variables as a fix for the functional-form problem and reports that the binary
version "typically displays larger biases than the continuous fraction affected or gap
specifications." AAIW's CCV needs binary treatment. So making CCV literally apply costs bite
accuracy. Both halves are in the menu; `ccv_applies_exactly` separates them.

Card (1992) introduced fraction-affected; Lee (1999) the effective-minimum-wage design; Card &
Krueger (1994) the gap measure.

## Clustering and shift-share inference

**Abadie, Athey, Imbens & Wooldridge (2023), QJE 138(1):1–35.** CCV. Reference implementation is
`Daniel-Pailanir/TSCB-CCV` (`ccv.ado`, `tscb.ado`), implementing eqs (13), (14), (20).

**Adão, Kolesár & Morales (2019), QJE 134(4):1949–2010.** Conventional standard errors
over-reject in shift-share designs — up to 55% at a 5% nominal level in their placebo exercise —
because residuals correlate across regions with similar exposure shares regardless of geographic
proximity. Their estimator needs many shocks of individually negligible relevance; there are 17
AEWR regions, so it does not apply. Their *insight* is implemented here as exposure-decile
clusters.

**Barrios, Diamond, Imbens & Kolesár (2012), JASA 107(498):578–591**, cited in AKM footnote 4:
when the shifter is as good as randomly assigned and independent across groups, clustering on
those groups is valid under any residual correlation structure. This is the justification for
G = 17.

**Borusyak, Hull & Jaravel (2022), REStud 89:181–213.** Shift-share validity resting on shock
exogeneity with endogenous shares; SSIV standard errors obtainable by estimating at the level of
identifying variation.

## The project's own documents (which turned out to matter more than the literature)

- `markdowns/predetermined_aewr_bite_design.md` — freeze `F_c^0`, never update with
  post-treatment wages; `B0_ct = ∫[AEWR_rt − max{w, M_ct}]_+ dF_c^0(w)`; state-by-year FE
  preferred, AEWR-region-by-year looser; "No specifications using contemporaneous local wages."
- `markdowns/ccv_extension.md` — the continuous-dose CCV with `Ω̂_g = (1/n_g) Σ D̃_gi²`, its
  binary reduction proof, the convex-combination proof, the unit-weighted variant, and its own
  §7 limitations.
- `markdowns/improved_dissimilarity_cluster_iv.md` — CZ-by-AEWR-region units, within-region
  agro-clustering on pre-sample primitives, region-varying cluster counts, minimum-mass
  constraints, "AEWR-region inference with few-cluster and weak-IV procedures", CR2.
- `markdowns/aewr_cluster_instrument_writeup.md` — the 17-FLS-region institutional setting; the
  bite `AEWR_r(i),t − w25_it`; why it is endogenous through FLS aggregation.
- `ccv_extension/ccv_proof/Lean/continuous_extension_proof_draft.md` — states plainly that the
  scalar reduction `Ω_g = W̄_g(1−W̄_g)` does **not** survive for continuous treatment and that the
  Lean development proves a covariance-kernel result, **not** that substituting a continuous
  within-cluster second moment into eq (20) is valid.

## One correction worth stating

`ccv_extension/ccv_proof/R/iv.R` is **not** a CCV implementation. `vcov_iv()` supports
IID / HC0 / HC1 / CLUSTER and computes a plain 2SLS sandwich `B M B'` on `X̂ = P_Q X` scores; the
CLUSTER branch is CR0/CR1. The label string "CCV IV cluster (CR1)" is a naming artefact. The
repo's CCV content is in the Lean files and the markdown, not in the R package.
EOF
cat > 99_open_questions.md << 'EOF'
# Open questions and known soft spots

1. **Continuous CCV is not proven.** `ccv_extension.md` §7 admits it: the formula is exact "under
   a continuous-dose assignment model where the cluster-level identifying-variation object Ω_g is
   sufficient (e.g. a common-shape location-scale assignment process). For arbitrary continuous
   treatments, higher moments and slope heterogeneity may affect the variance." The Lean draft is
   blunter still. Every continuous-dose CCV number in the menu inherits that.

2. **Rhode Island.** Five RI counties are absent in 2009, so the `f0809` frozen window is a
   one-year mean for them and a two-year mean everywhere else. This is unresolved item 21 from the
   prior session's own list. Currently silent in the code; needs a predeclared rule.

3. **The wage percentiles are all-occupation, not agricultural.** `predetermined_aewr_bite_design.md`
   wants agricultural and low-wage-worker distributions as sensitivities. Those distributions are
   not in this parquet, so the bite is built on the overall distribution only.

4. **`aewr_cz_p25` was never reverse-engineered.** It is not `AEWR/w_p25` (correlation 0.61 with
   that ratio, and it takes negative values), it has no metadata description, and the build code
   for it was not located. It is carried in the menu under its own label as an opaque
   repo-supplied bite, flagged as contemporaneous-wage.

5. **`post = 1{year ≥ 2017}` is arbitrary.** It exists only to manufacture a binary treatment so
   AAIW eq (20) applies literally. There is no single AEWR break; the AEWR moves every year. The
   `cum` and `d1` shocks are the honest ones and the `post` family should be read as "what CCV
   says when you force the design into the shape CCV requires."

6. **Sample-splitting CCV (eqs 13/14) is not implemented.** Only the closed-form FE variant
   (eq 20) is. `ccv.ado`'s OLS branch uses repeated random half-sample splits; that is a different
   estimator and would need `pk` as well as `qk`.

7. **`q = 1` throughout** — all 17 regions observed, per "everything is observed". If the estimand
   is a larger population of possible regions, `q < 1` raises λ toward 1 and pushes CCV toward the

# Prior art — searched before designing, not after

## Bite / fraction-affected designs

**Haanwinckel (2024), arXiv 2307.01284, "Does regional variation in wage levels identify the
effects of a national minimum wage?"** The on-point methodological critique. Canonical exposures:

```
FA_r  = (1/I_r) Σ_i 1{ w_i0 < mw_1 }
Gap_r = Σ_i max{ mw_1 − w_i0, 0 } / Σ_i w_i0
```

Three named failure modes: (1) sensitivity to the functional form of the treatment-intensity
variable; (2) regression to the mean at the regional level, from sampling variation in regional
wage statistics and from region-specific productivity shocks; (3) trends in the dispersion of
latent wages (e.g. skill-biased technical change) violating parallel trends *even when they hit
every region identically*. Fix for (2) is the Dustmann et al. (2021) procedure — construct the
bite from a different pre-period than the one anchoring the outcome.

**The finding that cuts against this whole exercise:** Haanwinckel tests binarised
treatment-intensity variables as a fix for the functional-form problem and reports that the binary
version "typically displays larger biases than the continuous fraction affected or gap
specifications." AAIW's CCV needs binary treatment. So making CCV literally apply costs bite
accuracy. Both halves are in the menu; `ccv_applies_exactly` separates them.

Card (1992) introduced fraction-affected; Lee (1999) the effective-minimum-wage design; Card &
Krueger (1994) the gap measure.

## Clustering and shift-share inference

**Abadie, Athey, Imbens & Wooldridge (2023), QJE 138(1):1–35.** CCV. Reference implementation is
`Daniel-Pailanir/TSCB-CCV` (`ccv.ado`, `tscb.ado`), implementing eqs (13), (14), (20).

**Adão, Kolesár & Morales (2019), QJE 134(4):1949–2010.** Conventional standard errors
over-reject in shift-share designs — up to 55% at a 5% nominal level in their placebo exercise —
because residuals correlate across regions with similar exposure shares regardless of geographic
proximity. Their estimator needs many shocks of individually negligible relevance; there are 17
AEWR regions, so it does not apply. Their *insight* is implemented here as exposure-decile
clusters.

**Barrios, Diamond, Imbens & Kolesár (2012), JASA 107(498):578–591**, cited in AKM footnote 4:
when the shifter is as good as randomly assigned and independent across groups, clustering on
those groups is valid under any residual correlation structure. This is the justification for
G = 17.

**Borusyak, Hull & Jaravel (2022), REStud 89:181–213.** Shift-share validity resting on shock
exogeneity with endogenous shares; SSIV standard errors obtainable by estimating at the level of
identifying variation.

- `markdowns/predetermined_aewr_bite_design.md` — freeze `F_c^0`, never update with
  post-treatment wages; `B0_ct = ∫[AEWR_rt − max{w, M_ct}]_+ dF_c^0(w)`; state-by-year FE
  preferred, AEWR-region-by-year looser; "No specifications using contemporaneous local wages."
- `markdowns/ccv_extension.md` — the continuous-dose CCV with `Ω̂_g = (1/n_g) Σ D̃_gi²`, its
  binary reduction proof, the convex-combination proof, the unit-weighted variant, and its own
  §7 limitations.
- `markdowns/improved_dissimilarity_cluster_iv.md` — CZ-by-AEWR-region units, within-region
  agro-clustering on pre-sample primitives, region-varying cluster counts, minimum-mass
  constraints, "AEWR-region inference with few-cluster and weak-IV procedures", CR2.
- `markdowns/aewr_cluster_instrument_writeup.md` — the 17-FLS-region institutional setting; the
  bite `AEWR_r(i),t − w25_it`; why it is endogenous through FLS aggregation.
- `ccv_extension/ccv_proof/Lean/continuous_extension_proof_draft.md` — states plainly that the
  scalar reduction `Ω_g = W̄_g(1−W̄_g)` does **not** survive for continuous treatment and that the
  Lean development proves a covariance-kernel result, **not** that substituting a continuous
  within-cluster second moment into eq (20) is valid.

`ccv_extension/ccv_proof/R/iv.R` is **not** a CCV implementation. `vcov_iv()` supports

CLUSTER branch is CR0/CR1. The label string "CCV IV cluster (CR1)" is a naming artefact. The
repo's CCV content is in the Lean files and the markdown, not in the R package.

input.file_text:
"""Reduce the menu to readable summaries."""

import polars as pl

MENU = "/mnt/user-data/outputs/h2a_ccv_menu.parquet"
OUT = "/mnt/user-data/outputs/h2a_ccv_summary.md"


def fmt(df: pl.DataFrame) -> str:
    with pl.Config(tbl_rows=200, tbl_cols=25, tbl_width_chars=200, set_fmt_float="full"):
        return str(df)


def main():
    m = pl.read_parquet(MENU)
    clean = m.filter(~pl.col("uses_contemporaneous_wages"))
    parts = [f"# H-2A sub-region bite menu — summary\n\n{m.height:,} rows; "
             f"{m.select(['family','outcome','exposure','baseline','form','shock','fe']).unique().height:,} "
             f"distinct specifications x {m['cluster'].n_unique()} cluster definitions.\n"]

    parts.append("\n## 1. SE ratios by cluster definition (predetermined exposures only)\n\n"
                 "How much each estimator moves relative to HC1, and what lambda does.\n\n")
    t1 = (
        clean.group_by("cluster")
        .agg(
            pl.col("n_clusters").median().alias("G"),
            (pl.col("se_cr1") / pl.col("se_hc1")).median().alias("cr1/hc1"),
            (pl.col("se_cr2") / pl.col("se_hc1")).median().alias("cr2/hc1"),
            (pl.col("se_cv3") / pl.col("se_hc1")).median().alias("cv3/hc1"),
            (pl.col("se_cv3_exact") / pl.col("se_hc1")).median().alias("cv3exact/hc1"),
            (pl.col("se_ccv_hc3_mean") / pl.col("se_hc1")).median().alias("ccvhc3/hc1"),
            (pl.col("se_ccv_hc3_mean") / pl.col("se_cr1")).median().alias("ccvhc3/cr1"),
            pl.col("ccv_lambda_hc3_mean").median().alias("lambda"),
            pl.col("omega_cv_hc3_mean").median().alias("omega_cv"),
        )
        .sort("G")
    )
    parts.append(fmt(t1))

    parts.append("\n\n## 2. Sign and significance by outcome x treatment family\n\n"
                 "Share of specifications with beta<0, and share with |t|>=3 under CCV-HC3.\n\n")
    t2 = (
        clean.filter(pl.col("cluster") == "aewr_region_id")
        .group_by("outcome", "family")
        .agg(
            pl.len().alias("specs"),
            (pl.col("beta") < 0).mean().alias("share_neg"),
            (pl.col("t_ccvhc3").abs() >= 3).mean().alias("share_t3_ccvhc3"),
            (pl.col("t_cv3x").abs() >= 3).mean().alias("share_t3_cv3exact"),
            pl.col("beta").median().alias("median_beta"),
        )
        .sort("outcome", "family")
    )
    parts.append(fmt(t2))

    parts.append("\n\n## 3. Where CCV applies exactly (binary treatment) vs by analogy\n\n")
    t3 = (
        clean.filter(pl.col("cluster") == "aewr_region_id")
        .group_by("ccv_applies_exactly")
        .agg(
            pl.len().alias("rows"),
            pl.col("ccv_lambda_hc3_mean").median().alias("lambda"),
            (pl.col("se_ccv_hc3_mean") / pl.col("se_cr1")).median().alias("ccvhc3/cr1"),
            (pl.col("se_ccv_cr1_hc3_mean") / pl.col("se_ccv_hc3_mean")).median().alias(
                "df_adj_effect"
            ),
        )
    )
    parts.append(fmt(t3))

    parts.append("\n\n## 4. Exposure ranking, region-clustered, CCV-HC3\n\n")
    t4 = (
        clean.filter((pl.col("cluster") == "aewr_region_id") & (pl.col("outcome") == "y_cert_pos"))
        .group_by("exposure")
        .agg(
            pl.len().alias("specs"),
            pl.col("beta").median().alias("median_beta"),
            (pl.col("beta") < 0).mean().alias("share_neg"),
            pl.col("t_ccvhc3").median().alias("median_t_ccvhc3"),
            pl.col("t_cv3x").median().alias("median_t_cv3exact"),
        )
        .sort("median_t_ccvhc3")
    )
    parts.append(fmt(t4))

    parts.append("\n\n## 5. Fixed-effect absorption\n\n")
    t5 = (
        clean.filter(pl.col("cluster") == "aewr_region_id")
        .group_by("fe")
        .agg(
            pl.len().alias("rows"),
            pl.col("beta").median().alias("median_beta"),
            (pl.col("beta") < 0).mean().alias("share_neg"),
            pl.col("t_ccvhc3").abs().median().alias("median_abs_t"),
        )
    )
    parts.append(fmt(t5))

    parts.append("\n\n## 6. Discarded contemporaneous-wage family vs frozen baseline\n\n")
    t6 = (

    )
    parts.append(fmt(t6))

    txt = "".join(parts) + "\n"
    open(OUT, "w").write(txt)

Four corrections, all landed. Here's where things stand.

**The JSONs.** I hadn't opened them; now converted to markdown in `work/transcripts/` via `extract_json.py`, which handles both export shapes (ChatGPT `mapping` graphs walked back from `current_node`, Claude `chat_messages` with thinking/tool_use/tool_result blocks). 2.66M chars across four files. The MCW conversation carries binding instructions I was violating: the inference target is **CCV-corrected HC3**, not CR1 and not CCV-HC0 — I had only HC0 as the robust component, now `{hc0, hc3} × {mean, unit}` weighting gives four CCV variants per row. Also `q=1` ("everything is observed"), no polynomial bases anywhere, polars never pandas, 2011-as-magic-year rejected, and the real object of interest is post-fit delta-method inference on constructed combinations rather than per-coefficient SEs — my menu is per-coefficient, which I've logged as an open gap rather than pretended away. The stated `|t| ≥ 3` under CCV-HC3 benchmark I'm reporting against, not steering toward; a 3,888-fit menu is precisely the instrument that could manufacture it.

**The repos, read properly this time.** `markdowns/predetermined_aewr_bite_design.md` explicitly discards `AEWR_rt − w25_ct` because the local quantile responds to local demand and to the AEWR itself through FLS aggregation, and directs "No specifications using contemporaneous local wages." My first-pass fa/gap/kaitz/czp25 exposures *were* the discarded design. Rebuilt around the repo's own object, `B0_ct = ∫[AEWR_rt − max{w, M_ct}]₊ dF_c⁰(w)` with the distribution frozen on 2008–09 and `M_ct` the state ag floor (mean $0.79/hr; FA0 mean 0.264), and added the state-by-year FE that note prefers and I'd omitted. The discarded family stays in the menu behind a `uses_contemporaneous_wages` flag so the discrepancy is measurable rather than assumed.

`markdowns/ccv_extension.md` caught a real error: Ω̂_g is the within-cluster mean **squared residualised** dose, and I'd implemented the variance of the raw treatment. Different object, and λ depends on it, so every CCV number would have been wrong. Fixed, then re-ran the `ccv.ado` equivalence test — CCV-HC0 0.0267434 against ado 0.02674343, λ 0.0003398 against 0.00033977. That note's §4 binary-reduction proof now holds numerically in my code, which is a stronger check than before because the Ω definition changed underneath it and the identity survived. `improved_dissimilarity_cluster_iv.md` gave the cluster construction: CZ-by-region units, within-region Ward clustering on pre-sample farm structure with K ∈ {2,3,5} (G = 34/49/81), minimum-mass folding, plus CR2 — which I derived for the scalar-after-FWL case as `Σ Ψ_g²/(1 − S_g/S)/S²`, the rank-one collapse of Bell-McCaffrey.

**No randomisation inference or bootstrap.** `run_ri.py` deleted, `design_ri()` stripped. Few-cluster robustness is CR2, CV3 in two versions, exact leave-one-cluster-out for G ≤ 60, and `t_{G−1}` only.

**tmux.** Using `tmux wait-for menudone` against the `-S` signal I'd already wired in, bounded by `timeout` so a single call can't hang the turn.

Nine deliberately overlapping docs in `work/docs/` (`00_START_HERE`, `10_design_decisions`, `20_treatment_definitions`, `30_cluster_definitions`, `40_inference_estimators`, `50_data_notes`, `60_prior_art`, `70_transcript_findings`, `99_open_questions`), plus the running trace.

Rhode Island's five counties are still missing 2009, which silently makes the `f0809` frozen window a one-year mean for them; unresolved, logged as open question 2.

The grid is at 2200/3888 fits, 30,758 rows, running under tmux. `summarize.py` is written and ready to run against it.

# Findings from the completed menu

54,096 rows = 3,864 distinct specifications x 14 cluster definitions.

## 1. The headline: at the theoretically correct cluster level, CCV collapses onto HC

Clustering on AEWR region (G = 17, the level of the shifter, the Barrios–Diamond–Imbens–Kolesár
justification):

```
lambda   = 0.022        omega_cv = 0.148
cr1/hc1  = 2.96         cv3_exact/hc1 = 2.88
ccvhc3/hc1 = 1.006      ccvhc3/cr1    = 0.373
```

lambda near zero means `V_CCV = lambda·V_cluster + (1−lambda)·V_robust` is ~98% robust. **CCV-HC3
at the region level is HC1 wearing a different name** — it is 2.7x *smaller* than CR1 and 0.6%
away from HC1. It is not a precision gain from better inference; it is `lambda -> 0` because
`Omega_g` is nearly constant across the 17 regions (`omega_cv` = 0.148, i.e. a 15% coefficient of
variation).

This is the correct AAIW answer, not a bug: with `q = 1` (all regions observed) and homogeneous
within-cluster identifying variation, there is no cluster-level design uncertainty left to price.
But it means every CCV-significant result in this menu needs to be read as an HC result.

## 2. What that does to the t >= 3 benchmark

Interact family, region-clustered:

| outcome | share \|t\| >= 3 under CCV-HC3 | under exact CV3 |
|---|---|---|
| `y_cert_pos` | 0.511 | 0.167 |
| `y_cert_hours` | 0.491 | 0.151 |
| `y_apps` | 0.516 | 0.193 |
| `y_ln_farm_emp` | 0.319 | 0.004 |

The benchmark is met three times as often under CCV-HC3 as under the exact cluster jackknife, and
the entire gap is the lambda collapse. Anyone reporting "t > 3 with CCV-HC3 standard errors"
should be asked for `lambda` and `omega_cv` in the same table.

## 3. lambda is a monotone function of how you draw clusters

| cluster | G | lambda | omega_cv | ccvhc3/cr1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aewr_region_id` | 17 | 0.022 | 0.148 | 0.373 |
| `agro2` | 34 | 0.104 | 0.341 | 0.499 |
| `agro3` | 49 | 0.139 | 0.401 | 0.545 |
| `state_fips` | 48 | 0.161 | 0.439 | 0.538 |
| `agro5` | 81 | 0.181 | 0.471 | 0.599 |
| `region_year` | 204 | 0.380 | 0.782 | 0.745 |
| `cz_region` | 694 | 0.446 | 0.898 | 0.764 |
| `state_year` | 576 | 0.516 | 1.032 | 0.806 |
| `county_fips` | 3,079 | 0.578 | 1.170 | 0.819 |

Same data, same beta; the CCV standard error moves by a factor of ~2.2 purely through cluster
definition, and it moves *monotonically in `omega_cv`* exactly as the algebra says it must.
Finer clusters -> more dispersion in `Omega_g` -> higher lambda -> CCV closer to cluster-robust.
This is the "how many clusters is a function of design" point in one table: the estimator is not
selecting a cluster level for you, it is amplifying whichever one you chose.

## 4. The strongest result is the most mechanically suspect

Exposure ranking on `y_cert_pos`, region-clustered:

| exposure | median beta | share neg | median t (CCV-HC3) | median t (CV3 exact) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `h2a` | −0.740 | 0.86 | **−19.5** | −7.19 |
| `h2apred` | −0.205 | 0.81 | −3.51 | −1.03 |
| `ZB0rel` (frozen) | −0.087 | 0.81 | −1.80 | −0.72 |
| `ZFA0` (frozen) | −0.095 | 0.86 | −1.80 | −0.64 |
| `slack` | −0.325 | 0.65 | −0.91 | −1.01 |
| `labint` | +0.159 | 0.15 | +3.29 | +1.10 |

parsed.body:
- Collaborating on an H-2A agricultural guest-worker paper examining AEWR effects
- Built a complete 78-page Typst/Touying slide deck for the paper
- Received an honest assessment of the research's structural gaps around substitution margins
- Estimation branch is the "multilevel Mundlak-Chamberlain-Wooldridge" design (design version 2.3.0), primary model id `chamberlain_rich`; R + fixest, 01_build_panel / 02_estimate_models / 03_postestimation / 04_diagnostics / 05_validate, plus design.R and helpers.R
- Continuous AEWR dose (100*Dlog AEWR) varies at AEWR-region-year level across 17 regions; inference uses a finite-design CCV with 17 cyclic path-reassignment states and t_16 critical values; Lean-formalized (see [[panel-econometrics-research]])
- Analysis years 2013-2022, baseline 2008-2010, treatment history 2011-2022; quadratic dose basis, lags 0-2; Z = standardized baseline AEWR bite
- Asked for evaluation of a proposed overhaul converting the design to fully saturated ETWFE with dose x all-baseline-covariate interactions
- Aug 10 2026: doing Mundlak-Chamberlain-Wooldridge work with three repos pulled together — ChurnKenLee/h2a_aewr_paper, ChurnKenLee/ccv_extension (Lean CCV proofs, see [[panel-econometrics-research]]), and py-econometrics/duckreg
- Considers the Wooldridge source material in `code/designs/mundlak_chamberlain` critical background for this work
- Reads the design as a parametric panel model, not an ETWFE instance: continuous always-on dose can't saturate, so you parameterize. Equation (1) = random-coefficients panel model Y = W*B_it + gamma_t + C_i + U_it with Chamberlain projection on C_i and a correlated-random-coefficient projection on B_it
- Position: richer parameterization handles the strict-exogeneity/feedback problem (AEWR set from FLS regional wages, so outcome innovations can enter future doses)
- Design decisions for the maximal MCW spec: NO separate pre-period year values (2008/2009/2010) in the projection, NO imposed linear trends, NO quadratic or cubic dose basis for now (linear dose only). Pre-period covariates enter as means at each hierarchy level
- More MCW spec decisions: interaction terms are fine and good; drop the arbitrary 3-year focal window {s, s-1, s-2} entirely (no causal-vs-nuisance split in the history block); per-term standard errors on every regression coefficient are unnecessary since inference is post-fit delta method on constructed combinations
- Rejected 3-lag history as garbage: "full history or one lag or bust". No logit or any nonlinear link anywhere in this work — OLS linear regression only (log/asinh transforms of variables are fine). Said interpretability degrading under full history means the implementation isn't being done properly, not that the spec is wrong
- REJECTED the cubic Almon lag profile as "some bullshit way to hide a three-lag window". No quadratic or cubic terms anywhere, including polynomial restrictions on the lag profile. Full history with every lag freely estimated; interaction terms remain fine and good
- CCV corrections to the standard errors must be applied properly (the residual-df adjustment was missing)
- The FLS-instrument / panel-IV route is NOT necessary for this work (said he would explain why later)
- Questions 2011 as a "magic year" — its use as the eligibility filter, the outcome normalizer (emp_farm_2011), and the baseline-covariate denominator is not well justified
- Aug 12 2026: wants a vast menu of candidate specifications built around sub-AEWR-region "bite" treatment definitions, so CCV estimation actually applies via within-region variation, crossed with many cluster definitions (how many clusters is a function of design/question/DGP). Explicitly: NO randomization inference and NO bootstrap of any kind

- Wants uploaded JSON conversation exports comprehensively parsed with jq/Python/ripgrep, and the GitHub repos actually browsed, before design work — both were things he had to ask for twice
- Inference target on this project is CCV-corrected HC3 (not CR1, not CCV-HC0), with q=1 since all 17 regions are observed; benchmark he named is |t| >= 3 on the core elasticity with the expected sign being H-2A usage falling as AEWR rises

Pattern: compress a read-only directory with `mksquashfs -comp zstd -Xcompression-level 6`, mount it read-only (`mount -t squashfs -o loop `), then layer a writable directory on top with `mount -t overlay overlay -o lowerdir=,upperdir=,workdir= ` so new writes land in the upper layer while unchanged-file reads come from the compressed lower layer. Verified end to end on a real ~1031-target Lean/mathlib build under live disk pressure: compression ratios of roughly 2.5x-5x on build artifacts and source, file counts and checksums matched exactly post-mount, and the build continued correctly (no spurious rebuilds, no corruption) once swapped into the live path. Two confirmed pitfalls from that session: (1) don't delete a package's `.git` directory to reclaim space — lake/git tooling can read that as tampering and trigger a full wipe-and-reclone of already-built artifacts; (2) a long-running compression/build job launched via a single blocking tool call can get killed mid-write by the tool's own execution-time limit and leave a plausible-looking but corrupted output file — always background long jobs (`setsid nohup ... &`, matching the persistence pattern already documented above) and verify the result (e.g. `dwarfsck`-equivalent integrity check, or just re-reading it back) rather than trusting that a reasonable file size means a clean finish.

The claim that these facts are worth persisting rests on an unverified assumption: that all conversations' sandboxes are provisioned from the same template/image, so template-level properties (resource limits, mount layout, tmux/SIGHUP mechanics) recur even though the instance doesn't. That's a reasonable inference from how such systems are normally built, not something confirmed by comparing containers across two actual conversations — I have no way to self-check it. To verify: in a fresh conversation, check `nproc`, `free -h`, the mount table, and disk headroom against the numbers below; a match confirms shared-template provisioning, a mismatch means this file should be reframed as "varies" rather than stated as fact. VERIFICATION RUN Aug 12 2026 in a separate conversation: `nproc`=1, ~3.9Gi RAM, `/` 252G nominal with ~10G available and 8.6G used — exact match on every number. Shared-template provisioning is now confirmed rather than assumed, so the template-level facts below can be treated as recurring - Bash tool calls are ephemeral in shell state only (env vars, cwd reset each call) — the underlying container/VM itself persists across calls and across turns within a session, confirmed via matching `boot_id` and `uptime -s` - This persistence is scoped to a single conversation only — near-certainly does not extend across separate conversations (each presumably gets its own fresh container; this session's own `uptime -s` showed boot only ~4s before the first command of this conversation, consistent with fresh-per-conversation provisioning, though never directly tested by opening a second conversation). The memory files are the actual cross-conversation persistence layer, not the sandbox — don't assume any running process, tmux session, or file written under /home/claude survives into a new conversation - For awaiting a tmux background job across separate bash tool calls, `tmux wait-for -S ` appended to the pane's command + `tmux wait-for ` from the awaiting call is confirmed-best: zero CPU while blocked, and race-free because the signal latches (fires instantly even if set before the wait began — tested by waiting 5s after job completion, still returned in ~6ms). Output-keyword polling (`capture-pane | grep`) has a confirmed false-positive hazard: tmux echoes the command line into the pane before it runs, so a completion keyword that also appears in the invoking command text matches immediately, before the job executes. Process-name polling (`pane_current_command` != shell name) is a safe fallback when the command can't be modified to emit a signal, but busy-waits for the duration. `monitor-silence`/`alert-silence` hooks did not fire in this sandbox in two tested configs (no attached client; script-faked attached+focused client) — not usable here. Practical addendum Aug 12 2026: a bare `tmux wait-for ` on a job longer than the bash_tool execution limit gets killed by that limit with no output, so wrap it as `timeout 250 tmux wait-for && echo DONE` and re-issue across calls — the latching property makes re-waiting free and race-free. Also, wiring `-S ` into the pane command and then polling with `sleep N` anyway is a real observed failure mode, not a hypothetical one. - Tested cross-turn persistence directly: launched a tmux-hosted heartbeat loop and a separate non-tmux `setsid`+`nohup` heartbeat loop, ended the turn, checked after the next prompt (~44s real elapsed time). Boot ID and `uptime -s` were unchanged, filesystem intact, and both logs showed continuous unbroken 2s-interval ticks straight through the turn boundary with no pause/freeze — the container was not recycled for this gap, and neither job needed tmux specifically to survive it (bare setsid+nohup did too). Turn boundaries alone do not recycle the sandbox; only tested a short (~44s) gap, so longer-gap or other-trigger recycling is untested, not ruled out. - Tested plain `cmd &` backgrounding with no setsid/nohup/disown/tmux, across bash_tool call boundaries: three separate jobs (40s, 30s, 90s) all ran to completion with no premature termination, confirmed via tick counts and a FINISHED marker line in each log. This contradicts a blanket "backgrounded processes don't survive between calls" — plain background jobs survive at least one call boundary fine here, likely because bash_tool runs each command non-interactively with no controlling terminal to send SIGHUP on exit. Never caught a job mid-flight to directly confirm reparenting to PID 1 — inter-call latency (30-90s+ observed) exceeded even the 90s test job's runtime each time. tmux/setsid remain the safer default for anything long or important, but a quick bare-backgrounded job isn't automatically unsafe here. - For the reasoning-trace-to-file practice (see /preferences.md): the persistent /home/claude directory is the right target, given the confirmed cross-call/cross-turn container persistence above — a trace file started early in a session can be appended to incrementally across the whole session rather than recreated per tool call - Filesystem: `/` (ext4, includes /home/claude and /tmp) reports 252G nominal device size but only ~10G actually available (8.6G used, `resv_strict` mount option) — treat ~10-19G as the real disk ceiling, not 252G. `/mnt/user-data/outputs` and `/mnt/user-data/uploads` are FUSE-mounted via rclone against a chat-scoped remote store (outputs rw, uploads ro), reporting 1.0P with 0 used — not local container disk, and presumably not subject to the same recycling as the container itself. `/mnt/skills/public` and `/mnt/skills/examples` are read-only squashfs. - Resource limits: single core (`nproc`=1), ~3.9GB total RAM (`free -h`), no swap. cgroup `memory.max`/`memory.limit_in_bytes` reports effectively unbounded (int64 max) via the legacy interface — misleading, actual RAM is the real ceiling. cgroup `cpu.cfs_quota_us` also reports unset (-1) despite the single-core reality, so don't trust cgroup values for capacity planning here, check `nproc`/`free` instead. `ulimit`: ~15953 max processes, 20000 open files, 8MB stack, core dumps disabled. - For disk-space pressure in this sandbox (e.g. large builds/installs eating the ~10-19G real ceiling): SquashFS + OverlayFS is the recommended default fix. Both are kernel-native here — confirmed `overlay` listed in `/proc/filesystems`, `mount -t squashfs -o loop` succeeds directly, no FUSE daemon involved — and `squashfs-tools` installs cleanly via apt in about a second. Pattern: compress a read-only directory with `mksquashfs -comp zstd -Xcompression-level 6`, mount it read-only (`mount -t squashfs -o loop `), then layer a writable directory on top with `mount -t overlay overlay -o lowerdir=,upperdir=,workdir= ` so new writes land in the upper layer while unchanged-file reads come from the compressed lower layer. Verified end to end on a real ~1031-target Lean/mathlib build under live disk pressure: compression ratios of roughly 2.5x-5x on build artifacts and source, file counts and checksums matched exactly post-mount, and the build continued correctly (no spurious rebuilds, no corruption) once swapped into the live path. Two confirmed pitfalls from that session: (1) don't delete a package's `.git` directory to reclaim space — lake/git tooling can read that as tampering and trigger a full wipe-and-reclone of already-built artifacts; (2) a long-running compression/build job launched via a single blocking tool call can get killed mid-write by the tool's own execution-time limit and leave a plausible-looking but corrupted output file — always background long jobs (`setsid nohup ... &`, matching the persistence pattern already documented above) and verify the result (e.g. `dwarfsck`-equivalent integrity check, or just re-reading it back) rather than trusting that a reasonable file size means a clean finish.

Menu is complete: 54,096 rows, 3,864 distinct specifications × 14 cluster definitions. The headline is a negative result, and it's the one that matters.

**At the only cluster level with a theoretical justification, CCV collapses onto HC.** Clustering on AEWR region (G=17, the shifter level, Barrios-Diamond-Imbens-Kolesár): λ = 0.022, ω_cv = 0.148. So CCV-HC3 comes out at 1.006× HC1 and 0.373× CR1. That's the correct AAIW answer given q=1 and near-homogeneous within-cluster identifying variation — there's no cluster-level design uncertainty left to price — but it means CCV-HC3 in this design is HC1 with a different name. Making CCV *apply* was achievable; making it *informative* was not.

What that does to your t ≥ 3 benchmark, region-clustered, interact family: 0.51 of specs clear it under CCV-HC3 versus 0.17 under the exact cluster jackknife. The entire 3× gap is λ. For `y_ln_farm_emp` it's 0.32 versus 0.004.

**λ moves monotonically with cluster choice, exactly as the algebra requires.** From 0.022 at G=17 up to 0.578 at G=3,079 counties, with ω_cv tracking it in lockstep (0.148 → 1.170) and the CCV/CR1 ratio going 0.373 → 0.819. Same β, same data; the CCV standard error swings by ~2.2× purely on how you drew the clusters. Your "how many clusters is a function of design" point lands as a warning rather than a menu of equally-valid options — the estimator amplifies whichever partition you handed it.

And the cruelest part: in the 368 rows where treatment is genuinely binary so eq (20) applies as derived, λ = 0.0022 — an order of magnitude *smaller*. Binarising within region at the median or upper quartile makes W̄_g(1−W̄_g) nearly equal across regions by construction. The construction that makes CCV valid is the construction that makes it uninformative.

**I checked the strongest result before reporting it.** `h2a` exposure gives median t = −19.5 under CCV-HC3. But that exposure is baseline certified H-2A per baseline farm worker, and the outcome is asinh(certified/emp_farm_2011×1000) — correlation between the exposure and the mean post-2011 outcome is 0.690. It's the baseline value of the outcome, so `h2a × shock` is a baseline-outcome-by-time interaction and the big negative coefficient is consistent with mean reversion, not a floor biting. `h2apred` is the same at one remove (0.440). The frozen bite B₀ is the only exposure not built from the outcome (−0.103) — and its |t| is under 2. Meanwhile `cropsh`/`farmsh`/`labint` carry the wrong sign with large t; they measure how agricultural a county is, not how hard the floor bites.

Two more things worth your attention. The repo's *preferred* absorption — county + state×year — is the one that kills the result: median |t| 1.73, share negative 0.46. The negative-sign majority lives in county+year, which doesn't absorb region-level AEWR shocks, so it's partly identified off the regional policy variation the bite design was supposed to condition away. And the discarded contemporaneous-wage bite produces the expected sign 77% of the time against 56% for the frozen one — the mechanical bias `predetermined_aewr_bite_design.md` warned about, showing up precisely as results that look right.

The residual-df adjustment is real but second-order here: `se_ccv_cr1/se_ccv` median is 1.012, because it multiplies a cluster component that λ has already nearly zeroed out.

Open gap I haven't closed: the delta-method layer. Your prior conversation is explicit that post-fit inference on constructed combinations is the object and per-coefficient SEs are unnecessary — this menu is per-coefficient. Wiring the CCV covariance into constructed elasticities is the obvious next piece, and it's where the λ problem will either bite harder or wash out depending on how the combinations weight the dose.

Close that, read much more of the relevant content of the JSONs using jq and ripgrep (be smart about filtering), optimize the code, and ***do not prioritize what is earlier in the JSONs over what is later***

def demean_warm(proj: FEProjector, X0: np.ndarray, tol: float = 1e-11, maxit: int = 200):
    """Alternating projections warm-started from already-nearly-residualised values.

    Used for leave-one-cluster-out refits: dropping one cluster barely moves the fixed-effect
    means, so the full-sample residuals restricted to the subsample are within a few sweeps of
    the subsample solution. This is the whole optimisation for exact CV3 — profiling showed 171
    cold refits per specification were 0.35s of a 0.58s evaluate().
    """
    X = np.array(X0, dtype=np.float64, copy=True)
    if X.ndim == 1:
        X = X[:, None]
    scale = max(float(np.abs(X).max()), 1e-12)
    sweeps = 0
    for _ in range(maxit):
        sweeps += 1
        if proj._sweep(X) < tol * scale:
            break
    return X, sweeps

gcl=rm.codes(d["aewr_region_id"])

    def n_params(self) -> int:''','''    def subset(self, mask: np.ndarray) -> "FEProjector":
        """Projector for a sub-sample, derived without re-sorting.

        A stable-sorted order filtered by a mask is still stably sorted, so the sub-sample's
        group structure comes from one boolean gather plus a run-length pass -- O(n) instead of
        the O(n log n) argsort that dominated the leave-one-cluster-out refits.
        """
        out = FEProjector.__new__(FEProjector)
        out.fes = []
        idx = np.flatnonzero(mask)
        remap = np.full(mask.size, -1, dtype=np.int64)
        remap[idx] = np.arange(idx.size)
        for order, starts, counts, keys in self.fes:
            keep = mask[order]
            new_order = remap[order[keep]]
            sorted_keys = np.repeat(keys, counts.astype(np.int64))[keep]
            if new_order.size == 0:
                out.fes.append((new_order, np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64), np.zeros(0), np.zeros(0)))
                continue
            new_starts = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, sorted_keys[1:] != sorted_keys[:-1]])
            new_counts = np.diff(np.r_[new_starts, sorted_keys.size]).astype(np.float64)
            out.fes.append((new_order, new_starts, new_counts, sorted_keys[new_starts]))
        out.n = int(idx.size)
        return out

    @property
    def n_params(self) -> int:''')
open(p,'w').write(s); print('patched')

input.file_text:
"""Post-fit delta-method inference on constructed combinations, against a multivariate CCV.

This closes the gap named in 99_open_questions.md item 8: the menu is per-coefficient, but this
project's stated object is post-fit delta-method inference on constructed quantities, with
per-coefficient standard errors explicitly declared unnecessary.

What is implemented
-------------------
V_CCV as a k x k matrix rather than a scalar:

    V_robust  = B [ sum_i d~_i d~_i' u~_i^2 / (1-h_i)^2 ] B      (HC3; HC0 drops the leverage)
    V_cluster = B [ sum_g Psi_g Psi_g' ] B,   Psi_g = sum_{i in g} d~_i u~_i
    Omega_g   = (1/n_g) sum_{i in g} ||d~_i||^2                  (trace form; scalar case is the
                                                                  formula in ccv_extension.md)
    lambda    = 1 - q (mean Omega)^2 / (mean Omega^2)
    V_CCV     = lambda V_cluster + (1-lambda) V_robust

Cross-outcome covariance is free in the same way the shared-state E matrices made it free in the
prior session: outcomes fitted on the same residualised design with the same clusters share B and
share the cluster partition, so

    V^{ab}_cluster = B [ sum_g Psi_g^a Psi_g^b' ] B

is a direct computation.  Stacking constructed quantities across outcomes then supports a joint
Wald test, a GLS-pooled common elasticity, and a test of the common-elasticity restriction.

Elasticity convention, taken verbatim from the project's own later reasoning
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    elasticity = 100 * (dY / d log-point) / mean(Y) = d ln Y / d ln AEWR, evaluated at the mean

with mean(Y) taken over the SAME population the partial effect is averaged over -- the earlier
error was averaging the effect over the active subpopulation while dividing by the mean over all
county-years including the zeros, and "a ratio whose numerator and denominator are taken over
different populations isn't an elasticity of anything".  mean(Y) is treated as FIXED, not as an
estimated quantity with its own gradient term, because under the design reference law
randomisation moves path assignment only, not the observed outcome means.

Not implemented: the 17-state cyclic (or full-permutation) reference law that generated the E
matrices in the prior session.  That is permutation resampling and is excluded this session.
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats


def ccv_matrix(Dt: np.ndarray, resid: dict, bread: np.ndarray, g: np.ndarray, qk=1.0,
               robust="hc3"):
    """Multivariate CCV for every outcome in `resid`, plus all cross-outcome blocks.

    Returns (V, lam, omega_cv) where V[(a, b)] is the k x k covariance block.
    """
    n, k = Dt.shape
    G = int(g.max()) + 1
    keys = list(resid)

    if robust == "hc3":
        H = np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", Dt, bread, Dt)
        wgt = 1.0 / np.maximum(1.0 - H, 1e-8) ** 2
    else:
        wgt = np.ones(n)

    # cluster scores per outcome: G x k
    Psi = {}
    for a in keys:
        sc = Dt * resid[a][:, None]
        P = np.zeros((G, k))
        for j in range(k):
            P[:, j] = np.bincount(g, weights=sc[:, j], minlength=G)
        Psi[a] = P

    Sg = np.bincount(g, weights=np.einsum("ij,ij->i", Dt, Dt), minlength=G)
    cnt = np.maximum(np.bincount(g, minlength=G), 1)
    omega = Sg / cnt
    m1, m2 = omega.mean(), (omega**2).mean()
    lam = float(np.clip(1.0 - qk * (m1**2 / m2), 0.0, 1.0)) if m2 > 0 else np.nan
    omega_cv = float(np.sqrt(max(m2 - m1**2, 0.0)) / m1) if m1 > 0 else np.nan

    V = {}
    for a in keys:
        for b in keys:
            meat_r = (Dt * (resid[a] * resid[b] * wgt)[:, None]).T @ Dt
            meat_c = Psi[a].T @ Psi[b]
            Vr = bread @ meat_r @ bread
            Vc = bread @ meat_c @ bread
            V[(a, b)] = lam * Vc + (1 - lam) * Vr
    return V, lam, omega_cv


def constructed(beta: dict, V: dict, contrasts: dict, scale: dict, df: int):
    """Delta method for scalar functionals c'beta * s, with the full cross-outcome covariance.

    contrasts: name -> (outcome, c) ; scale: outcome -> multiplier (e.g. 100/mean(Y)).
    Returns the stacked estimate vector, its covariance, and a per-quantity table.
    """
    names = list(contrasts)
    q = np.array([scale[o] * float(c @ beta[o]) for o, c in (contrasts[n] for n in names)])
    Vq = np.empty((len(names), len(names)))
    for i, ni in enumerate(names):
        oa, ca = contrasts[ni]
        for j, nj in enumerate(names):
            ob, cb = contrasts[nj]
            Vq[i, j] = scale[oa] * scale[ob] * float(ca @ V[(oa, ob)] @ cb)
    se = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.diag(Vq), 0.0))
    tab = []
    for i, nm in enumerate(names):
        t = q[i] / se[i] if se[i] > 0 else np.nan
        crit = stats.t.ppf(0.975, max(df, 1))
        tab.append(
            {
                "quantity": nm,
                "outcome": contrasts[nm][0],
                "estimate": q[i],
                "se": se[i],
                "t": t,
                "p": float(2 * stats.t.sf(abs(t), max(df, 1))) if np.isfinite(t) else np.nan,
                "ci_low": q[i] - crit * se[i],
                "ci_high": q[i] + crit * se[i],
                "df": df,
            }
        )
    return q, Vq, tab


def joint_wald(q: np.ndarray, Vq: np.ndarray, df: int):
    """Wald test that every stacked quantity is zero, with the small-G F conversion."""
    m = q.size
    Vi = np.linalg.pinv(Vq, rcond=1e-12)
    W = float(q @ Vi @ q)
    F = W * (df + 1 - m) / (m * df) if df + 1 - m > 0 else np.nan
    p = float(stats.f.sf(F, m, df + 1 - m)) if np.isfinite(F) and df + 1 - m > 0 else np.nan
    return {"wald": W, "F": F, "df1": m, "df2": df + 1 - m, "p": p}


def pool_common(q: np.ndarray, Vq: np.ndarray, df: int):
    """GLS pooling under a common-value restriction, plus a test of that restriction."""
    m = q.size
    Vi = np.linalg.pinv(Vq, rcond=1e-12)
    one = np.ones(m)
    denom = float(one @ Vi @ one)
    if denom <= 0:
        return {}
    pooled = float(one @ Vi @ q) / denom
    vp = 1.0 / denom
    res = q - pooled
    Wr = float(res @ Vi @ res)
    Fr = Wr * (df + 1 - m) / ((m - 1) * df) if m > 1 and df + 1 - m > 0 else np.nan
    crit = stats.t.ppf(0.975, max(df, 1))
    sd = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.diag(Vq), 1e-300))
    corr = Vq / np.outer(sd, sd)
    return {
        "pooled": pooled,
        "se": np.sqrt(vp),
        "t": pooled / np.sqrt(vp),
        "ci_low": pooled - crit * np.sqrt(vp),
        "ci_high": pooled + crit * np.sqrt(vp),
        "restriction_F": Fr,
        "restriction_p": (
            float(stats.f.sf(Fr, m - 1, df + 1 - m))
            if np.isfinite(Fr) and df + 1 - m > 0
            else np.nan
        ),
        "gls_weights": (Vi @ one / denom).tolist(),
        "min_offdiag_corr": float(np.min(corr[~np.eye(m, dtype=bool)])) if m > 1 else np.nan,
        "max_offdiag_corr": float(np.max(corr[~np.eye(m, dtype=bool)])) if m > 1 else np.nan,
    }

    elasticity = 100 * (dY / d log-point) / mean(Y) = d ln Y / d ln AEWR, evaluated at the mean

with mean(Y) taken over the SAME population the partial effect is averaged over -- the earlier
error was averaging the effect over the active subpopulation while dividing by the mean over all
county-years including the zeros, and "a ratio whose numerator and denominator are taken over
different populations isn't an elasticity of anything".  mean(Y) is treated as FIXED, not as an
estimated quantity with its own gradient term, because under the design reference law
randomisation moves path assignment only, not the observed outcome means.

Not implemented: the 17-state cyclic (or full-permutation) reference law that generated the E
matrices in the prior session.  That is permutation resampling and is excluded this session.
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats


def ccv_matrix(Dt: np.ndarray, resid: dict, bread: np.ndarray, g: np.ndarray, qk=1.0,
               robust="hc3"):
    """Multivariate CCV for every outcome in `resid`, plus all cross-outcome blocks.

    Returns (V, lam, omega_cv) where V[(a, b)] is the k x k covariance block.
    """
    n, k = Dt.shape
    G = int(g.max()) + 1
    keys = list(resid)

    if robust == "hc3":
        H = np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", Dt, bread, Dt)
        wgt = 1.0 / np.maximum(1.0 - H, 1e-8) ** 2
    else:
        wgt = np.ones(n)

    # cluster scores per outcome: G x k
    Psi = {}
    for a in keys:
        sc = Dt * resid[a][:, None]
        P = np.zeros((G, k))
        for j in range(k):
            P[:, j] = np.bincount(g, weights=sc[:, j], minlength=G)
        Psi[a] = P

    Sg = np.bincount(g, weights=np.einsum("ij,ij->i", Dt, Dt), minlength=G)
    cnt = np.maximum(np.bincount(g, minlength=G), 1)
    omega = Sg / cnt
    m1, m2 = omega.mean(), (omega**2).mean()
    lam = float(np.clip(1.0 - qk * (m1**2 / m2), 0.0, 1.0)) if m2 > 0 else np.nan
    omega_cv = float(np.sqrt(max(m2 - m1**2, 0.0)) / m1) if m1 > 0 else np.nan

    V = {}
    for a in keys:
        for b in keys:
            meat_r = (Dt * (resid[a] * resid[b] * wgt)[:, None]).T @ Dt
            meat_c = Psi[a].T @ Psi[b]
            Vr = bread @ meat_r @ bread
            Vc = bread @ meat_c @ bread
            V[(a, b)] = lam * Vc + (1 - lam) * Vr
    return V, lam, omega_cv


def constructed(beta: dict, V: dict, contrasts: dict, scale: dict, df: int):
    """Delta method for scalar functionals c'beta * s, with the full cross-outcome covariance.

    contrasts: name -> (outcome, c) ; scale: outcome -> multiplier (e.g. 100/mean(Y)).
    Returns the stacked estimate vector, its covariance, and a per-quantity table.
    """
    names = list(contrasts)
    q = np.array([scale[o] * float(c @ beta[o]) for o, c in (contrasts[n] for n in names)])
    Vq = np.empty((len(names), len(names)))
    for i, ni in enumerate(names):
        oa, ca = contrasts[ni]
        for j, nj in enumerate(names):
            ob, cb = contrasts[nj]
            Vq[i, j] = scale[oa] * scale[ob] * float(ca @ V[(oa, ob)] @ cb)
    se = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.diag(Vq), 0.0))
    tab = []
    for i, nm in enumerate(names):
        t = q[i] / se[i] if se[i] > 0 else np.nan
        crit = stats.t.ppf(0.975, max(df, 1))
        tab.append(
            {
                "quantity": nm,
                "outcome": contrasts[nm][0],
                "estimate": q[i],
                "se": se[i],
                "t": t,
                "p": float(2 * stats.t.sf(abs(t), max(df, 1))) if np.isfinite(t) else np.nan,
                "ci_low": q[i] - crit * se[i],
                "ci_high": q[i] + crit * se[i],
                "df": df,
            }
        )
    return q, Vq, tab


def joint_wald(q: np.ndarray, Vq: np.ndarray, df: int):
    """Wald test that every stacked quantity is zero, with the small-G F conversion."""
    m = q.size
    Vi = np.linalg.pinv(Vq, rcond=1e-12)
    W = float(q @ Vi @ q)
    F = W * (df + 1 - m) / (m * df) if df + 1 - m > 0 else np.nan
    p = float(stats.f.sf(F, m, df + 1 - m)) if np.isfinite(F) and df + 1 - m > 0 else np.nan
    return {"wald": W, "F": F, "df1": m, "df2": df + 1 - m, "p": p}


def pool_common(q: np.ndarray, Vq: np.ndarray, df: int):
    """GLS pooling under a common-value restriction, plus a test of that restriction."""
    m = q.size
    Vi = np.linalg.pinv(Vq, rcond=1e-12)
    one = np.ones(m)
    denom = float(one @ Vi @ one)
    if denom <= 0:
        return {}
    pooled = float(one @ Vi @ q) / denom
    vp = 1.0 / denom
    res = q - pooled
    Wr = float(res @ Vi @ res)
    Fr = Wr * (df + 1 - m) / ((m - 1) * df) if m > 1 and df + 1 - m > 0 else np.nan
    crit = stats.t.ppf(0.975, max(df, 1))
    sd = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.diag(Vq), 1e-300))
    corr = Vq / np.outer(sd, sd)
    return {
        "pooled": pooled,
        "se": np.sqrt(vp),
        "t": pooled / np.sqrt(vp),
        "ci_low": pooled - crit * np.sqrt(vp),
        "ci_high": pooled + crit * np.sqrt(vp),
        "restriction_F": Fr,
        "restriction_p": (
            float(stats.f.sf(Fr, m - 1, df + 1 - m))
            if np.isfinite(Fr) and df + 1 - m > 0
            else np.nan
        ),
        "gls_weights": (Vi @ one / denom).tolist(),
        "min_offdiag_corr": float(np.min(corr[~np.eye(m, dtype=bool)])) if m > 1 else np.nan,
        "max_offdiag_corr": float(np.max(corr[~np.eye(m, dtype=bool)])) if m > 1 else np.nan,
    }

"""Delta-method layer: constructed combinations with multivariate CCV standard errors.

Two specifications per (exposure, cluster, FE) cell:

  dynamic   D = [ E_c x 1{year = t} ]_{t != base}.  Every year freely estimated, no polynomial
            basis, no imposed lag profile.  Constructed: average post effect, average pre effect
            (placebo), post minus pre.
  dose      D = [ E_c x cumulative log AEWR change ].  Scalar; the elasticity per log point.

Both are estimated on the full sample and on the active subpopulation, with the elasticity
denominator taken over whichever population the effect was averaged over.
"""

import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/claude/work/h2a_ccv")
import deltamethod as dm  # noqa: E402
import fastfwl as ff  # noqa: E402
from run_menu import FRAME, codes, within_group_transform  # noqa: E402

OUT_TABLE = "/mnt/user-data/outputs/h2a_ccv_delta_method.parquet"
OUT_MD = "/mnt/user-data/outputs/h2a_ccv_delta_method.md"

OUTCOMES = ["y_apps", "y_cert_pos", "y_cert_hours", "y_ln_farm_emp"]
DEMAND = ["y_apps", "y_cert_pos", "y_cert_hours"]
EXPOSURES = {
    "ZB0_f0809": "frozen dollar bite, 2008-09 baseline",
    "ZB0rel_f0809": "frozen bite / AEWR",
    "ZFA0_f0809": "frozen fraction affected",
    "slack_b0810": "AEWR headroom over the state ag floor",
    "labint_b0810": "hired-labor expense share",
}
CLUSTERS = ["aewr_region_id", "state_fips", "agro3", "cz_region", "county_fips"]
FE_SETS = {"county+year": ("county", "year"), "county+stateyear": ("county", "state_year")}
PRE_YEARS = (2011, 2012, 2013)
POST_YEARS = (2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022)


def build_cell(df, exposure_col, region_code, base_scalars):
    e_raw = base_scalars[exposure_col]
    return within_group_transform(e_raw, region_code, "cont_z_region")


def main():
    df = pl.read_parquet(FRAME).filter(pl.col("year") >= 2011)
    n = df.height
    yrs = df["year"].to_numpy()
    cty = df["county_fips"].to_numpy()
    region_code = codes(df["aewr_region_id"])

    base = {}
    m11 = yrs == 2011
    for c in ["B0_f0809", "B0rel_f0809", "FA0_f0809"]:
        lut = dict(zip(cty[m11], df[c].to_numpy()[m11]))
        base["Z" + c] = np.array([lut.get(k, np.nan) for k in cty])
    for c in ["slack", "labint"]:
        base[f"{c}_b0810"] = df[f"E_{c}_b0810"].to_numpy()

    fe_arrays = {
        "county": codes(df["county_fips"]),
        "year": codes(df["year"]),
        "state_year": codes(df["state_year"]),
    }
    cluster_arrays = {c: codes(df[c]) for c in CLUSTERS}
    shock = df["shock_cum"].to_numpy()
    ys = {o: df[o].to_numpy() for o in OUTCOMES}
    active = df["nbr_workers_certified_start_year"].to_numpy() > 0

    year_vals = sorted(set(yrs.tolist()))
    rows, pooled_rows = [], []
    t0 = time.perf_counter()

    for exposure in EXPOSURES:
        e_all = np.full(n, np.nan)
        okE = np.isfinite(base[exposure])
        e_all[okE] = within_group_transform(base[exposure][okE], region_code[okE], "cont_z_region")

        for sample in ("all", "active"):
            smask = okE & (active if sample == "active" else np.ones(n, bool))
            for o in OUTCOMES:
                smask = smask & np.isfinite(ys[o])
            if smask.sum() < 4000:
                continue

            means = {o: float(ys[o][smask].mean()) for o in OUTCOMES}
            scale = {o: (100.0 / means[o] if abs(means[o]) > 1e-9 else np.nan) for o in OUTCOMES}

            for feset, fekeys in FE_SETS.items():
                proj = ff.FEProjector([fe_arrays[k][smask] for k in fekeys])
                Y = np.column_stack([ys[o][smask] for o in OUTCOMES])

                for spec in ("dynamic", "dose"):
                    if spec == "dynamic":
                        cols, labels = [], []
                        for t in year_vals:
                            if t == PRE_YEARS[0]:
                                continue
                            cols.append(e_all[smask] * (yrs[smask] == t))
                            labels.append(int(t))
                        D = np.column_stack(cols)
                    else:
                        D = (e_all[smask] * shock[smask])[:, None]
                        labels = ["dose"]

                    M = proj.demean(np.column_stack([Y, D]))
                    Yt, Dt = M[:, : len(OUTCOMES)], M[:, len(OUTCOMES) :]
                    keep = np.linalg.norm(Dt, axis=0) > 1e-8
                    Dt, labels = Dt[:, keep], [l for l, k in zip(labels, keep) if k]
                    if Dt.shape[1] == 0:
                        continue
                    beta, resid, bread = {}, {}, None
                    for j, o in enumerate(OUTCOMES):
                        b, r, bread = ff.ols_multi(Yt[:, j], Dt)
                        beta[o], resid[o] = b, r

                    for cname in CLUSTERS:
                        gc = np.unique(cluster_arrays[cname][smask], return_inverse=True)[1]
                        G = int(gc.max()) + 1
                        df_t = G - 1
                        V, lam, ocv = dm.ccv_matrix(Dt, resid, bread, gc, 1.0, "hc3")
                        Vh, _, _ = dm.ccv_matrix(Dt, resid, bread, gc, 1.0, "hc0")

                        contrasts, k = {}, Dt.shape[1]
                        if spec == "dynamic":
                            post = np.array([1.0 if l in POST_YEARS else 0.0 for l in labels])
                            pre = np.array([1.0 if l in PRE_YEARS else 0.0 for l in labels])
                            if post.sum() == 0 or pre.sum() == 0:
                                continue
                            post /= post.sum()
                            pre /= pre.sum()
                            for o in OUTCOMES:
                                contrasts[f"avg_post::{o}"] = (o, post)
                                contrasts[f"avg_pre::{o}"] = (o, pre)
                                contrasts[f"post_minus_pre::{o}"] = (o, post - pre)
                        else:
                            c1 = np.ones(k)
                            for o in OUTCOMES:
                                contrasts[f"elasticity::{o}"] = (o, c1)

                        q, Vq, tab = dm.constructed(beta, V, contrasts, scale, df_t)
                        _, _, tab0 = dm.constructed(beta, Vh, contrasts, scale, df_t)
                        se_hc0 = {r["quantity"]: r["se"] for r in tab0}
                        for r in tab:
                            rows.append(
                                {
                                    "exposure": exposure,
                                    "sample": sample,
                                    "fe": feset,
                                    "spec": spec,
                                    "cluster": cname,
                                    "n_clusters": G,
                                    "n": int(smask.sum()),
                                    "ccv_lambda": lam,
                                    "omega_cv": ocv,
                                    "quantity": r["quantity"].split("::")[0],
                                    **{kk: vv for kk, vv in r.items() if kk != "quantity"},
                                    "se_ccv_hc0": se_hc0[r["quantity"]],
                                }
                            )

                        if spec == "dose":
                            idx = [
                                i
                                for i, nm in enumerate(contrasts)
                                if nm.split("::")[1] in DEMAND
                            ]
                            qd, Vd = q[idx], Vq[np.ix_(idx, idx)]
                            jw = dm.joint_wald(qd, Vd, df_t)
                            pc = dm.pool_common(qd, Vd, df_t)
                            pooled_rows.append(
                                {
                                    "exposure": exposure,
                                    "sample": sample,
                                    "fe": feset,
                                    "cluster": cname,
                                    "n_clusters": G,
                                    "ccv_lambda": lam,
                                    **{f"joint_{kk}": vv for kk, vv in jw.items()},
                                    **{
                                        kk: vv
                                        for kk, vv in pc.items()
                                        if kk != "gls_weights"
                                    },
                                    "gls_weights": str(
                                        [round(w, 3) for w in pc.get("gls_weights", [])]
                                    ),
                                }
                            )
        print(f"{exposure} done {time.perf_counter() - t0:.0f}s rows={len(rows)}", flush=True)

    tab = pl.DataFrame(rows)
    tab.write_parquet(OUT_TABLE)
    pool = pl.DataFrame(pooled_rows)
    pool.write_parquet(OUT_TABLE.replace(".parquet", "_pooled.parquet"))

    with pl.Config(tbl_rows=80, tbl_cols=20, tbl_width_chars=200, set_fmt_float="full"):
        md = ["# Delta-method inference on constructed combinations\n",
              f"\n{tab.height:,} constructed-quantity rows; {pool.height:,} pooled rows.\n",
              "\n## Elasticities per log point of AEWR, region-clustered, CCV-HC3\n\n",
              str(tab.filter((pl.col("quantity") == "elasticity")
                             & (pl.col("cluster") == "aewr_region_id"))
                  .select("exposure", "sample", "fe", "outcome", "estimate", "se", "t",
                          "ci_low", "ci_high", "ccv_lambda")
                  .sort("exposure", "sample", "fe", "outcome")),
              "\n\n## Dynamic profile: post vs pre placebo, region-clustered\n\n",
              str(tab.filter((pl.col("spec") == "dynamic")
                             & (pl.col("cluster") == "aewr_region_id")
                             & (pl.col("outcome") == "y_cert_pos"))
                  .select("exposure", "sample", "fe", "quantity", "estimate", "se", "t")
                  .sort("exposure", "sample", "fe", "quantity")),
              "\n\n## Cross-outcome pooling of the three demand margins\n\n",
              str(pool.select("exposure", "sample", "fe", "cluster", "n_clusters", "joint_F",
                              "joint_p", "pooled", "se", "t", "restriction_F", "restriction_p",
                              "max_offdiag_corr", "gls_weights")
                  .sort("cluster", "exposure", "sample", "fe")),
              "\n"]
    open(OUT_MD, "w").write("".join(md))
    print("".join(md)[:4000])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

cd /home/claude/work/docs && cat > 90_delta_method.md << 'EOF'
# Delta-method layer — closing the per-coefficient gap

The menu is per-coefficient. This project's stated object is post-fit delta-method inference on
constructed combinations, with per-coefficient standard errors explicitly declared unnecessary.
`h2a_ccv/deltamethod.py` + `h2a_ccv/run_delta.py` close that.

## What was built

**Multivariate CCV.** `V_CCV = lambda V_cluster + (1-lambda) V_robust` as a `k x k` matrix:

```
V_robust  = B [ sum_i d~_i d~_i' u~_i^2 / (1-h_i)^2 ] B        (HC3; HC0 drops the leverage term)
V_cluster = B [ sum_g Psi_g Psi_g' ] B,   Psi_g = sum_{i in g} d~_i u~_i
Omega_g   = (1/n_g) sum_{i in g} ||d~_i||^2                    (trace form of ccv_extension.md)
lambda    = 1 - q (mean Omega)^2 / (mean Omega^2)
```

**Cross-outcome covariance for free.** In the prior session this came from the 17 shared
reassignment states — the `E[q]` matrices, `proj = E[q] @ g`, `V = Pm'Pm/17`. Here it comes from
the same place analytically: outcomes fitted on the same residualised design with the same cluster
partition share `B` and share the partition, so `V^{ab}_cluster = B [sum_g Psi_g^a Psi_g^b'] B` is
a direct computation. That supports a joint Wald test, a GLS-pooled common elasticity, and a test
of the common-elasticity restriction, exactly as before.

**Elasticity convention, taken from the project's own later reasoning:**

```
elasticity = 100 * (dY / d log-point) / mean(Y) = d ln Y / d ln AEWR, evaluated at the mean
```

with the denominator over the **same population** the effect is averaged over. The earlier error
was averaging over the active subpopulation while dividing by the mean over all county-years
including the zeros; every mean is ~1.5x larger on the active subpopulation, so that inflated the
magnitudes by ~35% while leaving `t` untouched. `mean(Y)` is treated as **fixed**, with no second
gradient term, because under the design reference law randomisation moves path assignment only,
not the observed outcome means.

**Two specifications.** `dynamic`: `D = [E_c x 1{year=t}]`, every year freely estimated, no
polynomial basis and no imposed lag profile; constructed quantities are the average post effect,
the average pre effect (placebo), and their difference. `dose`: `D = E_c x cumulative log AEWR
change`, giving the elasticity per log point.

**Not rebuilt:** the 17-state cyclic reference law (and the full-permutation comparison the prior
session ran alongside it). That is permutation resampling, excluded this session. The CCV here is
analytic throughout.

## Results

### The placebo passes, and post-minus-pre clears t = 3

`y_cert_pos`, frozen bite `ZB0_f0809`, region-clustered (G = 17), CCV-HC3, full sample:

| FE | avg_pre | avg_post | post − pre |
|---|---|---|---|
| county + year | +0.283 (t 0.22) | −2.474 (t −2.18) | **−2.757 (t −3.52, p 0.003)** |
| county + state×year | +0.073 (t 0.05) | −2.497 (t −1.94) | −2.571 (t −2.72, p 0.015) |

The pre-period placebo is flat for every exposure tested (|t| < 0.8 throughout). Under the
county+year absorption the post-minus-pre difference clears the stated `|t| >= 3` benchmark. Under
the repo's preferred state-by-year absorption it does not (t = −2.72).

### But a placebo-passing t > 3 also exists with the wrong sign

`labint_b0810` (hired-labor expense share), full sample, county+year: avg_pre +0.793 (t 0.56) —
placebo passes — and post − pre = **+4.553, t = +5.37**. `slack_b0810` gives −6.875, t = −5.25.
A flat pre-trend does not discriminate between these; three exposures pass the placebo and
disagree in sign and magnitude by a factor of two.

### The sign is an extensive-margin result

Pooled demand elasticity across applications / certified positions / certified hours, `ZB0_f0809`,
region-clustered:

| sample | FE | pooled | se | t | restriction F | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | county+year | **−4.514** | 1.669 | −2.71 | 5.21 | 0.020 |
| all | county+state×year | −4.362 | 2.144 | −2.03 | 2.38 | 0.129 |
| active | county+year | **+2.121** | 0.863 | +2.46 | 0.92 | 0.420 |
| active | county+state×year | +0.099 | 0.980 | +0.10 | 0.15 | 0.866 |

Restricting to county-years with positive H-2A activity **flips the sign**. The negative response
lives entirely on the extensive margin — counties moving to and from zero — not on the intensive
margin of how much H-2A a user of the programme requests.

### The common-elasticity restriction, and why pooling cannot rescue precision

On the active subpopulation the restriction that all three demand margins share one elasticity is
**not rejected** (F = 0.92, p = 0.42), reproducing the prior session's finding (F = 1.24). On the
full sample it **is** rejected (F = 5.21, p = 0.020). The three margins correlate 0.93–0.99 across
clusters — even tighter than the 0.41–0.87 the prior session measured across reassignment states —
so GLS assigns negative weights (−1.896 on one margin for `slack`, −0.554 for `labint`), the
classic near-collinear signature. Pooling near-duplicate estimators cannot manufacture information.

### lambda is still small

Across the delta-method cells, region-clustered `lambda` runs 0.021–0.084. So CCV-HC3 here is
again close to HC3, and the same reading applies as in `80_findings.md`: the constructed-quantity
standard errors are essentially heteroskedasticity-robust ones, not cluster-design ones.
EOF
cat > 91_optimisation.md << 'EOF'
# Optimisation — what was measured, including what didn't work

`cProfile` on a single `evaluate()` call, before changing anything:

```
0.583s total
  0.347s   171 x fit_scalar          <- the exact leave-one-cluster-out CV3 refits
    0.318s   inside demean
  0.164s   355 x np.unique           <- re-uniquing FE codes for every leave-one-out subsample
  0.025s   56  x ccv
```

So exact CV3 was ~60% of runtime. Three candidate fixes were implemented and benchmarked; **two of
the three did nothing**, and reporting that is the point:

| change | measured | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| group-sorted `np.add.reduceat` demeaner, all columns in one vectorised call | 0.3x on one column, 1.1x on 40 | the original per-column `bincount` loop was already fine |
| warm-starting leave-one-out from the full-sample residuals | 2.0 sweeps instead of ~30, beta identical to 1e-16, **1.0x wall clock** | convergence sweeps were never the cost |
| `FEProjector.subset()` deriving sub-sample group structure from the filtered sorted order, O(n) instead of a fresh argsort | 0.9–1.0x at G = 12, 17, 48, 49 | sorting was never the cost either |

The 7ms per refit is raw per-call array overhead — fancy-index gather and scatter over a 31k x 2
array — not sorting, not sweeps, not convergence. The only lever that moves the total is doing
**fewer refits**.

## What was actually changed

1. `CV3_EXACT_MAX_G` from 60 to 20. Exact CV3 is now computed for `aewr_region_id` (17),
   `year` (12) and `expdec` (10) — 39 refits per specification instead of 170. Those are the
   cluster definitions where CV3 versus CR1 actually matters; at G = 48+ the two agree closely.
2. `cv3_exact_over_fwl` is now a reported column wherever both are computed, so the calibration
   between the exact jackknife and the cheap FWL-conditional one is auditable rather than assumed
   from the single 98.2% figure measured on simulated data.
3. Residualised outcomes cached per (sample mask, FE set): the outcome was being demeaned 3,888
   times when there are only a handful of distinct (mask, FE set) pairs.
4. `FEProjector` cached on the same key, and jobs sorted by FE set then outcome so cache hits are
   contiguous.
5. Leave-one-out refits now use `proj.subset(mask)` + `demean_warm`, avoiding the 355 `np.unique`

Correctness is checked by re-running the full grid and comparing point estimates and every
